meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give Owen a zero, and why wasn't I called first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. People draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale. Did anyone ask Owen that before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That's one timestamp log, not a finding. Whatever comes of it, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Different editions word things differently, and he may have the act wrong. Search the whole play, Hale, not one scene.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then search the whole text, now, with the screen turned to me.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
You still haven't searched the play. And students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's what outlines are for. What else is on that screen?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Nothing on his record, in writing tonight, that much I'll hold you to. I'm not agreeing to a rewrite while you still won't search that play in front of me. Do it, then we'll talk about the rest.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
You're scheduling past my question. The search, Hale, or there's no Thursday.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you admitted entering Owen's zero on November 3 without contacting me, and you committed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require you to search the entire text of Hamlet for the line you say is not in the play, and the zero withdrawn, before I agree to any rewrite. I expect that written commitment from you tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she holds you to keeping it off his record but has not accepted the rewrite, and she still wants you to search the whole play in front of her, so the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was within reach but not reached.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times and answered her drafted-elsewhere defence by inviting a dated draft, which gave her a specific, checkable record she couldn't wave away.
What cost ground: When she asked you to search the whole play, you moved on to the outline and then to scheduling, so your strongest second piece never stood and she refused the deal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the work between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on an October night, very close to that memory, and while it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The moment she asked you to search the whole play, run that search on the screen before showing the outline or offering 4.4.
